label: late copy-phase steps (last 1-2 outputs) whose input is l/v/r/i/m/n/p/o/h
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, never at recall_idx 0, and only on repeated inputs, in_first=0). It is concentrated on the last outputs of the sequence: to_go=0 holds 57% of the mass and to_go=1 holds 27%. It never fires with to_go>=6. Within those steps it strongly prefers certain fed-back input letters: l, v, r, i, m, n (rate 12-20%, 2.3-3.9x lift), then p, o, h. The largest activations are short sequences (L=3) at the final step with input v, m, r or w (e.g. q v o <DEL> q [v]). Short L (3-4) raises the rate. Position-only (copy & to_go<=1) gives recall 0.79 but precision 0.25; adding the token set raises precision to ~0.55 but lowers recall, so the token preference is graded rather than a clean set. The dev F1 plateaus at ~0.53, so this is only a partial explanation.
